title: Bootstrap by game: the market's MLB calibration is statistically perfect
headline_insight: Resampling whole games 1000 times, 0 of 10 MLB market probability bins deviate from the diagonal beyond noise, while the model misses in 3 of 10 -- worst in the 0.2-0.3 band, where 0.2449-forecasts come in at 0.1065 (gap -0.1384).
what_it_means: A cluster bootstrap (resampling game_id, 1000 draws) asks which calibration gaps survive sampling noise. For the market, none do -- its in-game MLB prices are indistinguishable from perfectly calibrated. The model has three real misses: it over-forecasts long shots in the 0.1-0.2 and 0.2-0.3 bands and under-forecasts the 0.8-0.9 band. The top bin is no longer a significant miss: 0.9516-forecasts win 0.9798, a gap of +0.0282 whose interval includes zero.
how_to_read: Each bin shows a gap (predicted minus actual) with a 95% confidence interval; if the interval excludes 0, the miss is real rather than noise.
why_it_matters: It separates genuine model weaknesses from statistical mirages, so improvement effort goes only to gaps that will still be there next month.
caveat: Soccer is much noisier -- 8 of 9 eligible model bins and 7 of 9 market bins deviate significantly on just 27 games, so the small corpus limits any firm conclusion there.
